title: The smallest useful inference
hypothesis: A minimal float32 Add graph can load and evaluate through the legacy WinRT CPU API in an x64 Xbox UWP app.

environment.hardware: Xbox Series S / Series X — not yet executed

reproduction: Implement the native C++/WinRT probe under issue #3, using pinned uwp-crossbuild and openappx; keep Probe.cs as an optional Windows reference.
Generate add.onnx using examples/generate_model.py and record its SHA-256.
Include the model and activation metadata in the x64 UWP layout; pack, sign and inspect with openappx.
Deploy through authenticated, certificate-pinned Device Portal and launch on each physical console without a debugger.
Export raw timing, correctness and environment logs with host/tool revisions, console provenance, source commit and artifact checksums.
limitations: No Xbox AI Lab execution evidence exists for this Add/WinML experiment.
Upstream source documentation reports a Series S launch and GGUF model load; that is not EXP-001 evidence, GPU validation or measured generation.
The native C++/WinRT port and lab cross-build are pending; Probe.cs is not directly compiled by uwp-crossbuild.
GPU execution is outside this experiment.
